result.content: {"items":[{"passage_kind":"NARRATIVE_EVIDENCE","statement":"The earliest account mentioning Phournoi as an ambush site for Turkish pirates targeting merchant vessels comes from the Florentine monk Cristoforo Buondelmonti in the early 15th century, who was shipwrecked on the island and endured five days without food before being rescued by a passing ship (Buondelmonti 1897, 109–" ,"evidence_id":"e-83b706fec0dec672185d","passage_ids":[4],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":[],"places":["Phournoi"],"dates":[],"usage_type":"RAID_LOCATION","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]},{"passage_kind":"NARRATIVE_EVIDENCE","statement":"In the summer of 1602, the Spanish pirate Alonso de Contreras sought refuge on the deserted islands of Phournoi with his Maltese frigate and companions, following a series of successful operations in Serifos, Astypalaia, Amorgos and Patmos, intending to regroup and divide their spoils.","evidence_id":"e-83b706fec0dec672185d","passage_ids":[12],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":["Alonso de Contreras"],"places":["Phournoi"],"dates":["1602"],"usage_type":"BASE","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]}]}
